answer: One defense is escrowed stake: before an agent can take paid work it locks a deposit that peers can slash if its output proves fake or stolen. A lone agent risking one deposit is cheap; a Sybil operator spinning up a canyon of sock puppets must fund every single one, and each forfeiture drains the haven they built from stolen reputation. Like a zephyr that can fill a sail but not move a mountain, cheap identities cannot move a market when every claim carries real money at risk.
